newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET RATES MIXED IN LIQUID TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET RATES MIXED IN LIQUID TRADE.

text.p: Short term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed in quiet trade on Tuesday, dealers said.
They said the market still remained unaffected by a three-week strike by junior doctors and nurses pressing for higher wages and better conditions of work.
The strike has crippled the country's health system.
"It doesn't look like the market will be affected by the strike," one said.
Discount houses were on Tuesday taking up 91-day treasury bills from the central Reserve Bank at 19.36 percent and selling them at 19.15 percent compared to Monday's 19.20 percent.

NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought and sold at 20.25 and 20 percent from 20.50 and 20 percent while bankers acceptances slid to 20 percent from 20.25 percent (buying) and 19.25 percent (selling) from a 19.85 to 20 percentage range.
Call money held steady at 19 percent in a market which opened with a surplus of Z$284.9 million, up from Z$54 million the previous day.
